Recorded precisely: the notice-retention sentence spans two physical lines ("...shall be included in all / copies or substantial portions of the Software."), which is template wrapping and not a textual variation.

thirdPartyBrandPosture.what: The application is an unaffiliated clone of Atlassian's Jira issue tracker: it reproduces Jira's board, issue-detail and search interaction model, and the upstream README describes it in those terms. The tree carries no Atlassian logo or product artwork; its icons are the project's own SVG set plus ng-zorro / Ant Design iconography.
thirdPartyBrandPosture.position: "Jira" is Atlassian's trademark. The upstream MIT grant covers the repository's own files; it is not treated here as any grant, permission or endorsement in respect of that mark. The application is carried as acquired upstream source and is not rebranded or presented as an Atlassian product.
thirdPartyBrandPosture.unknownPreserved: Whether the upstream project's use of the name is permitted, and on what basis, is neither established nor disclaimed by this record.

embeddedThirdPartyIdentifiers.what: The source carries a Google Analytics measurement id in src/app/core/services/google-analytics.service.ts and a Sentry DSN wired through @sentry/angular, both belonging to the upstream author, plus a Storybook GA id in the build-storybook script.
embeddedThirdPartyIdentifiers.position: These are upstream's own analytics identifiers, recorded here as a property of the acquired source. They are not credentials and grant no access; they are not reproduced in this evidence file.
embeddedThirdPartyIdentifiers.consequence: Any later unit that serves this fixture in a browser would, unmodified, report page views to the upstream author's analytics property. Recorded as a risk in admission.json rather than silently patched.
